Title: R&D Learning & Capability Development Manager
Industries to Target: Pharmaceuticals / Biotechnology / Life Sciences R&D; Semiconductors / AI Research / Advanced Materials / Photonics / Advanced Manufacturing
Position List EN: R&D Learning & Development Manager; R&D L&D Manager; Scientific Training Manager; R&D Academy Lead; Capability Development Lead; R&D Capability Manager; L&D Business Partner for R&D; Learning & Development Business Partner (R&D); Talent Development Manager; Learning Programme Manager; Early Careers Manager; Graduate Development Manager; Scientist Development Manager; Researcher Development Lead; Organization Development Manager (R&D); Strategic Development Manager (Science/R&D)
Notes:
WHO: Found in pharma, biotech, deep-tech with 100+ R&D staff. Direct report to Chief Scientific Officer, VP R&D, or Chief Learning Officer.

WHEN: Target when company has visible L&D program, research academy, or scientist development initiative. Best in large orgs with repeated training needs.

WHAT: Owns research training calendars, external provider evaluation, learning budgets. Decision maker for team-based workshops and multi-cohort programs.

WHY: These buyers recognize training gaps in researcher communication and actively search for specialist providers.

APPLY CLAY FILTERS:
- PRIMARY: Life Sciences Innovation Leaders (Filter 1)
- PRIMARY: Deep-Tech Innovation Leaders (Filter 2)
- SECONDARY: Research-Intensive Organizations (Filter 3)

NOTE: Do NOT require 'R&D' or 'Scientific' in job title. Look for generic L&D, Learning Programme, Talent Development, or Capability roles WITH evidence the person supports R&D/scientific populations. Check LinkedIn for R&D reporting structure and training focus.

Title: R&D Leadership with Budget Authority
Industries to Target: Pharmaceuticals / Biotechnology / Life Sciences R&D; Semiconductors / AI Research / Advanced Materials / Photonics / Advanced Manufacturing
Position List EN: VP of R&D; Head of R&D; Director of R&D; Research Director; VP of Research; Head of Research; Site Head; Chief Scientific Officer; CSO; VP Scientific Affairs; Head of Research Operations; Director of Research Operations; Chief Research Officer; VP Scientific Operations; Director of Scientific Affairs; Distinguished Scientist (R&D focus)
Notes:
WHO: Research leaders with direct budget authority over R&D teams. Found in larger pharma, biotech, deep-tech organizations or mid-sized biotech where R&D is core.

WHEN: Target when: (1) No dedicated L&D role exists for scientists; (2) Research leader sponsoring pilot training program; (3) Multi-site organization where site head controls local training budget; (4) Company is growing R&D and building capability infrastructure.

WHAT: May own or influence training budget, approve external partnerships, sponsor pilot programs with internal teams. Cares about researcher capability, retention, and competitive technical advantage.

WHY: Research leaders seeking to improve team capabilities and succession planning. More strategic than L&D buyers - think about long-term team development.

APPLY CLAY FILTERS:
- PRIMARY: Life Sciences Innovation Leaders (Filter 1)
- PRIMARY: Deep-Tech Innovation Leaders (Filter 2)
- SECONDARY: Research-Intensive Organizations (Filter 3)

NOTE: In site-based organizations (Roche, Boehringer, etc.), the relevant buyer may sit at individual research site rather than global headquarters. Target site heads with local autonomy.

Title: Scientific Programmes & Event Organizers
Industries to Target: Pharmaceuticals / Biotechnology / Life Sciences R&D; Semiconductors / AI Research / Advanced Materials / Photonics / Advanced Manufacturing
Position List EN: Scientific Communications Manager (internal); Scientific Communications Lead; Research Programme Manager; R&D Programme Manager; Research Symposium Manager; Technical Community Lead; Research Academy Manager; Poster Day Organizer; Senior Scientist (programme lead); Principal Scientist (training lead); Scientific Communications Director; Technical Community Manager; Research Community Manager; Internal Communications Manager (Science); Publications Manager (R&D)
Notes:
WHO: Found across research organizations, managing internal scientific events, poster sessions, research symposia, technical forums, or internal communication programs.

WHEN: Target when organizing: (1) Annual research symposia with 50+ researcher presentations; (2) Poster days with significant researcher participation; (3) Internal research academy or technical development program; (4) Cross-team technical communication forum; (5) Research bootcamp or new researcher onboarding.

WHAT: Organizes defined researcher cohorts/events. Often controls event budgeting and speaker/trainer selection. NOT always the final budget owner, but excellent champion for identifying needs and routing to decision maker.

WHY: Programme managers see researcher communication challenges firsthand (dense posters, unclear presentations) and actively seek solutions.

APPLY CLAY FILTERS:
- PRIMARY: Life Sciences Innovation Leaders (Filter 1) - when they organize structured events
- PRIMARY: Deep-Tech Innovation Leaders (Filter 2) - when they organize technical forums
- SECONDARY: Research-Intensive Organizations (Filter 3) - secondary markets with visible programmes

NOTE: Useful entry point but route to decision maker (L&D or research leadership) before proposing company-wide engagement. Ask about next cohort dates, participant numbers, and who approves training budget.
